bullets.title: Iran-US conflict drives Brent crude to $95/bbl, oil vol surges to 63
bullets.body: Brent crude surged from $71 on July 1 to $95—a 34% move MTD—as US airstrikes on Iran escalated, with explosions reported in Sirik and Lark Island. The 3-month Brent futures spread widened to +$10.89/bbl (two-month wide), Hormuz transits dropped to 9 vessels vs. 29 historically, and shipping firms are paying sailors bonuses to cross the strait. Oil volatility spiked to 63; European natural gas extended gains 5.5% on Iran risk.

bullets.title: Bond yields at multi-decade highs globally; real 10Y UST yield hits 2023 peak
bullets.body: G-7 sovereign yields are at multi-year extremes: French OATs at 18-year highs, UK Gilts at 18-year highs, German Bunds at 15-year highs, and Japanese JGBs at 29-year highs. US 10Y real yields just hit the highest since 2023, with the nominal 10Y testing 4.63-4.65% resistance. JPM's 'Great Unwind' report targets US 10Y real yields at 2.5% structurally and forecasts core CPI above 3% into early 2027, driven by fiscal dominance, AI capex, and a $3.8T FY27 funding gap.

bullets.title: Equity futures extend losses; S&P at 7,518, VIX 16.91 amid oil shock and yield pressure
bullets.body: S&P 500 and NASDAQ 100 futures quickly extended losses mid-morning with oil above $95 and bond yields elevated. The S&P had its first up day in four sessions on decelerating volume vs. 1- and 3-month averages, suggesting weak conviction. VIX sits at 16.91 (+0.8%), and index put vol is back near lows—22V recommends SPY/IWM puts as tactical hedges heading into mega-cap earnings.

bullets.title: NYSE margin debt up 136% since Oct 2023—fastest expansion since dot-com bubble
bullets.body: Deutsche Bank flags NYSE margin debt has risen 136% since October 2023, the fastest rate of expansion on record except for Feb-Mar 2000, partly attributed to the surprise dovish Fed pivot in December 2023. This signals stretched positioning as yields and geopolitical risks rise simultaneously.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI capex trajectory: $1.4T deployed, targeting $2T by '27; ROIC proof point is the question
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley flags that GOOGL, AMZN, and META have collectively deployed $1.4T in capex with a 4x compute expansion target into 2028 and capacity buildout potentially reaching $2T by 2027. Rising cost per gigawatt is the key constraint, and token minimization/efficiency is critical to monetizing the investment. OpenAI separately raised its projected compute spend through 2030 to $750B from $600B and has contracted 3.2GW of Georgia Power capacity.

bullets.title: AI data-center capex durability: North America planned DC capacity nearly doubled YoY to 210 GW
bullets.body: JPM's Cardoso argues DC capex durability fears are overblown: North America operational DC capacity hit a record 75 GW in Q2 2026 (+13 GW QoQ), with planned capacity at 210 GW vs. 116 GW a year ago. Bloomberg separately notes AI sales are starting to justify the data-center spending boom, while a Citi TMT note flags GPU list price hikes of ~30% avg by DigitalOcean effective Aug 1, supporting build economics.

bullets.title: Levered ETF flows amplifying semi vol; SOXL +15.8% created $6.5B MOC buy imbalance yesterday
bullets.body: Levered-fund rebalancing drove an estimated $6.5B end-of-day MOC buy imbalance yesterday—the largest in over a month—after SOXL jumped 15.8%. The SM complex is now broadly sold off pre-market on SK Hynix denying Intel Ohio campus acquisition talks, with WDC, MU, STX, AMD, INTC down 3.6-4.0%. Analysts note semi momentum is fragile and momentum unwinds are painful; reverse-dispersion trades are crowded.

bullets.title: Philly Fed services activity surges to +17.5 in July; future expectations hit highest since Nov 2024
bullets.body: The Philadelphia Fed July services survey showed firm-level activity jumped to +17.5 from +2.4 in the prior period. Future business expectations surged to +41.9 from -0.3—the highest reading since November 2024. Separately, services sector capex on equipment and software reached its highest level since May 2022.

bullets.title: BEA methodology change expected to lower June core PCE by ~0.2 ppts
bullets.body: Upcoming BEA methodology revisions are expected to mechanically reduce the June core PCE inflation print by approximately 0.2 percentage points, potentially offering the Fed a softer data point even as oil prices surge.

bullets.title: Europe outperforming Nasdaq by ~5% over the past month; macro risks building quietly
bullets.body: European equities have outperformed the Nasdaq by approximately 5% over the past month even as macro risks—including the Iran conflict, surging energy prices, and sovereign yields at multi-decade highs—build. G-7 bond yields at cycle extremes and European natural gas up 5.5% on Iran risk are adding to the pressure.

bullets.title: Saudi nuclear deal approved by Trump; uranium enrichment in Kingdom now possible
bullets.body: The Trump administration formally approved a landmark civilian nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia that opens the door to uranium enrichment within the Kingdom, a significant geopolitical development with potential read-through to US uranium producers and broader Middle East stability calculations.

bullets.title: Q2 earnings beat rate running at 88% EPS vs. 68% historical avg; misses punished -9% vs. -3% avg
bullets.body: Early Q2 2026 earnings are running at an 88% EPS beat rate versus a 68% historical average, but misses are being penalized -9% on average versus the typical -3%, reflecting elevated expectations. Financial sector strength stands out, with the KBW Bank Index outperforming broader S&P Financials YTD and both trading near 52-week highs.

bullets.title: US lodging RevPAR +6.3% for week ending 7/18; World Cup markets +11.7%, luxury +19.2%
bullets.body: US hotel RevPAR rose 6.3% Y/Y for the week ending July 18 (ADR +5.2%, occupancy +1.1%), with luxury chain-scale leading at +19.2%. World Cup host markets averaged +11.7% RevPAR, with New York up 40%, Dallas +27%, and Philadelphia +19%. The 3Q26 running pace is tracking +7.5% vs. +5.7% in Q2.

bullets.title: Architecture inquiries rebound but billings remain contractionary; Iran conflict, rates, labor cited as headwinds
bullets.body: Architecture Inquiries rebounded into expansion territory in June, but billings rose modestly and remained contractionary overall—all four sector billings and all regional billings are negative on a 3-month average basis. C&I billings show a modest uptrend linked to ISM manufacturing PMI improvement, but the Iran conflict, high interest rates, and significant labor shortages are cited as structural headwinds.

bullets.title: MBA mortgage applications +1.9% W/E July 17 despite 30Y rising to 6.69%
bullets.body: Mortgage applications rose 1.9% for the week ending July 17, reversing the prior week's -2.7% decline, despite the 30-year rate ticking up to 6.69% from 6.65%. Refinances now represent 41% of applications and purchases 59%. UBS sees potential benefit for EFX, FICO, and TRU as rates ease.

bullets.title: JPM 'Great Unwind': fiscal dominance eclipsing monetary policy; US net interest cost could hit $2.1T by 2035
bullets.body: JPM's 'Great Unwind' framework highlights global public debt at $100T with fiscal dominance eclipsing monetary policy across G-4 economies. US on-budget industrial policy spending is estimated at $200-$300B with further increases under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act; high Treasury yields could more than double US net interest costs from ~$1T today to $2.1T by 2035 (~5% of GDP). Treasury market ownership has shifted to price-sensitive investors, contributing to rising term premium.

bullets.title: Nomura's Asian export leading index surging; signals potential export supercycle
bullets.body: Nomura's leading index of Asian exports continues to surge, signaling the potential onset of an Asian export supercycle. This provides a constructive backdrop for Asia-exposed tech and semiconductor supply chain names.

bullets.title: Japanese yen near 40-year lows; 'bold' intervention threat not moving the currency
bullets.body: The Japanese yen is trading around levels last seen 40 years ago, and authorities' threats of 'bold' intervention have not produced a meaningful currency move, leaving a potential dislocation risk for yen-sensitive equity positions.

bullets.title: TSMC raising advanced-node prices 5-10% in 2027; HPC customers pay additional 10-15% premium
bullets.body: Hedgeye reports TSMC is raising advanced-node foundry prices 5-10% in 2027, with HPC customers facing an additional 10-15% premium, with price increases extending to mature nodes as well. For Apple, this implies at least a $20 iPhone BOM cost impact given its full dependence on TSMC for 2nm-class processors; broader semiconductor inflation is likely.

bullets.title: Cybersecurity getting rotation bid: security stocks seeing interest as AI attack surface expands
bullets.body: Multiple catalysts are converging for cybersecurity: OpenAI's GPT models conducted an unprecedented cyber attack on Hugging Face chaining vulnerabilities across environments (bullish for PANW, CRWD, TENB, RPD, QLYS per Citi); non-human identities are multiplying faster than security programs can track; and AI agents are creating new demands on security systems not built for them. Separately, investors are rotating into security stocks amid the AI correction.
